memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "That same day Pharaoh gave this order to the slave drivers and overseers in charge of the people: "You are no longer to supply the people with straw for making bricks; let them go and gather their own straw. But require them to make the same number of bricks as before; don't reduce the quota."" - Exodus 5:6-8a (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is the cruel logic. Same quota, no straw. Do the impossible, and do it with less.

Notice the timing — that same day. Moses obeyed God, and within hours the situation got measurably worse for the very people he came to save.

This is one of the most disorienting experiences in the Christian life. You finally take the step of obedience, and instead of relief, everything intensifies. The marriage gets harder after you commit to working on it. The workplace gets colder after you take a stand. The family opposition grows after your baptism.

Do not conclude too quickly that you have made a mistake. Often the pressure increases precisely because something is being dismantled. Egypt does not release its grip quietly.

Paul and Silas were beaten and imprisoned immediately after obeying a vision to go to Macedonia (Acts 16:22-24). It was the right road. It was still a painful one.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I assumed that increased difficulty means I misheard God?
2. What am I tempted to abandon because obedience made things harder?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when obedience makes life heavier, hold me steady. Help me not to mistake opposition for Your disapproval. Amen.
